title: End-to-end contracts for partial-object streaming and tool-call semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define clear, testable acceptance criteria and an implementation contract for emitting partial structured objects during response streaming, plus the exact semantics for invoking external tools/functions (sync vs async), error propagation, idempotency, and resume behavior.
background: Customers using streaming structured responses need reliable semantics when the model emits partial JSON or invokes tool calls mid-stream. Current behavior has ad-hoc heuristics across SDKs: some clients drop partial objects, others attempt to patch; tool invocation errors are surfaced inconsistently. This causes integration flakes for customers building long-running orchestrations or deterministic ingestion pipelines.
scope_changes: Initial spike scoped to chat/generation endpoints and function/tool-calling path. Does NOT include embeddings, batch inference, or Dedicated routing policies. If accepted, follow-up ticket will extend contract to SDK language bindings and Dedicated private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming payload format: define and document a canonical wire format for partial-object emission over streams (NDJSON envelope where each line is an event with type and lexically-valid JSON payload).

Partial-object contract: an event type 'partial' must include a 'path' (JSON Pointer as string) and 'patch' (RFC 6902 patch array as string-encoded JSON) or 'fragment' (stringified JSON fragment). Clients MUST be able to reconstruct final object using ordered application of received patches/fragments.

Complete-object event: an explicit 'complete' event must be emitted when a top-level structured object is finished. Receiving a 'complete' guarantees object is schema-valid against the negotiated schema version for that stream.

Schema negotiation: on request metadata, client MAY include 'schema-version' or 'schema-hint'. Server must include 'schema-version' in initial stream-open event. If versions mismatch, server must emit a 'schema-warning' event and follow graceful degradation rules below.

Tool-call initiation: tool/function calls must be emitted as events with type 'tool-call' containing a stable 'call_id' (UUID v4 string), 'tool_name', 'args' (JSON string), and 'expected_response_mode' (synchronous | async | fire-and-forget).

Tool-call response semantics: for synchronous mode, a 'tool-result' event with matching 'call_id' MUST precede the enclosing object's 'complete' event. For async, 'tool-ack' then optionally later 'tool-result' events are allowed; clients must rely on 'call_id' to correlate results.

Idempotency and retries: servers must treat identical tool-call events with the same 'call_id' as idempotent; clients may retry by resending same 'call_id'. Tool providers must expose an idempotency key mapping if backend requires it.

Error propagation: errors from tool invocation MUST be emitted as 'tool-error' with 'call_id', 'error_code' (standardized string), and human 'message'. For transient errors the server should include 'retry_after' (seconds).

Resume and recovery: streams must support a 'resume_token' emitted at regular checkpoints. Clients can reconnect and resume from a token; server guarantees at-least-once delivery of events after the token. Resume behavior must be documented and tested.

Backpressure and pacing: when server detects slow consumers, it must emit 'throttle' events indicating suggested pacing (ms). Client SDKs must expose hooks for honoring 'throttle' and expose observable metrics when not honoring.

Validation and finality: on 'complete' event server must include 'schema-validation' field (pass | fail) and, if fail, an array of validation hints. The stream-level exit code must be one of success | partial | error.
Backward compatibility: protocol must allow adding new event types and fields; unknown event types must be ignored by clients but logged. Version negotiation must be explicit in stream-open event.

End-to-end tests: acceptance requires automated tests that simulate partial emission, mid-stream tool failures, connection interrupts and resume tokens; tests must run in CI and assert deterministic reconciliation of final objects.
Docs & examples: publish a minimal spec doc plus sample replayable transcripts (NDJSON) and SDK snippet demonstrating reconstruction and resumption in both Node and Python clients.
Migration guidance: provide a short guide for existing customers, including opt-in header 'X-RI-structured-stream=v1' and a deprecation plan for legacy heuristic behavior.
out_of_scope: Wire-format change for non-streaming API responses
Runtime routing/fallback policies for Dedicated clusters
Language SDK full rewrites (only example snippets are in scope)
proposed_design: Adopt an NDJSON event envelope with a small set of canonical event types: stream-open, partial, tool-call, tool-ack, tool-result, tool-error, schema-warning, throttle, resume_token, complete, stream-close. Each event must include monotonically increasing 'seq' integer. Provide a lightweight JavaScript/Python reference reconstructor that applies patches/fragments in order and validates final object against the schema using JSON Schema draft-07.
implementation_steps: Define formal event schema and publish spec draft in docs repo
Instrument runtime to emit stream-open and seq numbers, implement resume token generator
Implement tool-call envelope and assign stable call_id for tool invocations from runtime
Add resume and replay hooks to connection manager and server-side checkpointing
Add CI tests that simulate intermittent connections and assert final object equivalence
Publish docs and SDK examples; coordinate announcement with SDK owners
test_plan: Unit tests for NDJSON event serializer/deserializer
Integration test: model runtime emits partial patches then complete; client reconstructs and validates
Chaos test: force TCP drop, reconnect with resume_token, assert no duplicate application beyond idempotency semantics
Tool-failure test: simulate transient and permanent tool errors and assert correct tool-error events and retry_after behavior
Performance test: measure throughput overhead of envelope vs baseline and validate <3% p99 token latency regression
risks: Client adoption friction: existing SDKs and customers may not implement patch-apply correctly leading to integration bugs
Operational complexity: checkpointing and resume tokens increase state burdens on runtime
Tool-provider incompatibility: third-party tools may not support idempotent retries without additional mapping
notes: 2026-03-03: Initial review with runtime team - flagged storage cost for long-lived resume tokens
2026-03-05: Design feedback - prefer JSON Patch (RFC 6902) for deterministic patches; fallback fragment mode allowed for streaming partial strings
2026-03-08: Security review requested - tool-call events may contain PII in args; mark for redaction guidance
2026-03-10: PM judgement - proceed with v1 that is conservative: event seq required, resume token optional but recommended
